doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing with legends and the rhythm guitarist's attitude
summary: Barker says he takes whatever he can do, since leaders want his rhythm rather than solos.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Then you recorded with quite a few other people, most recently, in recent years, Wynton Marsalis. What was it like recording with such a wide range of people, going from some of the early jazz pioneers to some of the latest up and coming . . .

You just go on. Something you think you can make, you make. If the people really want you, they’ll go with what you do. You don’t be running up and grabbing things where they’re going to give you some virtuoso music to read technically. I don’t do that, because I can’t. I don’t see that far with music. I’m playing rhythm guitar, and I go along with that. What was your question again?
I was asking, what was it like to play with so many legendary people up until . . .
You go and play. Most of them will accept me, because most of them want the solos. What I would do, they would like to have that. So you can have that. You go and play.
